newsitem.title: UK: Coffee trade watches deliveries after price surge.
newsitem.headline: Coffee trade watches deliveries after price surge.

text.p: Coffee traders said they were watching out for producer defaults after being alerted by reports in the market that a small cargo from Vietnam for a European destination had failed to meet a shipment deadline.
The Vietnam cargo was only a few hundred tonnes and some traders said that, in this particular case, failure to meet the contract deadline could simply be the result of a hold up at the port.

But traders said that a surge of 30 percent in the price of Robusta coffee since the beginning of January might tempt some producers to try to re-negotiate sale contracts agreed at lower price levels. "There is a bit of panic around," said one, adding that the market was now on an alert for signs of default, mainly from Far Eastern origins.
"This is nothing new. It happens all the time when prices rally so much," a trader said.
Market sources reckon Vietnam must have sold about half of its coffee crop.
